content:
.
..
.claude
.engramdb
.git
Makefile
README.md
flags.toml
migrations
pyproject.toml
scripts
src
tests
.PHONY: test test-fast

test-fast:
	pytest -m "not postgres" -q

test:
	pytest -q

To cut a release, you push a git tag named `vYYYY.MM.N` and CI handles the build and publish. Don't publish by hand.

```sh
git checkout main && git pull
make test                    # full suite, including the Postgres tests
git tag v2026.10.1           # year.month.N, e.g. the first release in October 2026
git push origin v2026.10.1
```

N counts releases within the month (the documented example is `v2026.09.2`).

This comes from a single team memory in the project's EngramDB notes. I couldn't confirm it against anything else in the repo:

- **No CI config in this checkout.** There's no `.github/workflows/` or similar, so I can't see which job builds on the tag, what it publishes, or where.
- **No tags exist yet.** I couldn't confirm the naming from past releases, or whether N starts at 1 or 0.
- **No release instructions in the repo.** The README and Makefile don't mention releasing. The Makefile only has `test` and `test-fast`.
- **Running tests first is my suggestion.** Nothing documented says it's required before tagging.

Before you push the first tag, ask whoever owns CI where the tag-triggered pipeline is defined. It may live outside this repo.
